technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot as the base application framework, extending the existing application that exposes endpoints at http://localhost:9393/.
Leverage Spring Security for all authentication mechanisms, configured via Java configuration classes rather than XML.
Adopt Spring Integration patterns for source/sink modules (U4, U6, U7, U8) to remain consistent with the existing 'jdbchdfs' module architecture.
For file-based security (U1), use Spring Security's InMemoryUserDetailsManager or a properties file-backed UserDetailsService.
For LDAP-based security (U2), use Spring Security LDAP with embedded UnboundID LDAP server support for local testing, and a configurable external LDAP URL for production.
Role hierarchy (U3): Admin (full access) > Viewer (read-only), enforced via Spring Security's hasRole() / hasAuthority() expressions and method-level @PreAuthorize annotations.

For Kerberized HDFS sink (U4), use Hadoop's UserGroupInformation.loginUserFromKeytab() to authenticate and obtain a delegation token, and follow existing HDFS sink code patterns but add Kerberos configuration (principal, keytab, krb5.conf).
For HBase sink (U6), use the Apache HBase client API directly (org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.*) rather than Spring Data, to keep dependencies minimal and match the existing sink style.
For File Roll sink (U7), use a rolling file strategy based on file size and/or time interval, modeled on logback/log4j rolling policies, writing to a configurable directory.
For JMX source (U8), use Spring Integration's JMX support (int-jmx: notification-listening-channel-adapter) to subscribe to MBean notifications and publish to a message channel.
U5 is explicitly a spike / research activity producing design specs only - no production code is delivered as part of this increment.
All modules will include unit tests (JUnit 5, Mockito) and integration test scaffolds; production deployment/infrastructure is out of scope.
assumptions: A single developer performs all development work described in the specification.
An existing application exists with endpoints exposed at http://localhost:9393/ and a 'jdbchdfs' sink module that serves as a reference for code style and module packaging.
The developer is familiar with Spring Boot, Spring Security, Spring Integration, and Hadoop ecosystem basics, but will need to learn specifics of HBase, Kerberos, and JMX integration on the job.

HBase, Kerberos KDC, and LDAP servers are not pre-provisioned; the developer will set up minimal local test instances (e.g., HBase in Docker, embedded LDAP, MIT Kerberos in a VM) for development and testing.
Production infrastructure, deployment automation, and CI/CD pipeline work are out of scope.
Configuration externalization (application.yml / properties) is used for all endpoints, credentials references, and module behavior.
Effort includes coding, unit tests, and self-verification, but not formal QA, code review cycles with multiple reviewers, or release management.
The mass-ingestion spike (U5) outputs a design document, not implementation; estimated effort covers research, prototyping, and documentation.
Documentation is concise developer-facing (README updates + sample configurations), not full user manuals.

activities.activity_description: Review the existing codebase, identify extension points for the new security layer and source/sink modules, define package structure, set up Maven/Gradle dependencies for Spring Security, Spring LDAP, Hadoop Kerberos, HBase client, and Spring Integration JMX.

Implement a Spring Security configuration class that supports file-based authentication (e.g., users/roles from application.yml or a separate properties file). Secure all endpoints at localhost:9393/. Provide example configuration and unit tests.

Implement a Spring Security LDAP configuration that authenticates users against an external LDAP server. Support configurable LDAP URL, base DN, user DN pattern, and group search. Include embedded LDAP fallback for local testing. Secure all endpoints. Add unit and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: U3: Default Access Control with Admin/Viewer Roles
activities.activity_description: Define Admin and Viewer roles, configure role-based access rules across endpoints (URL-based via HttpSecurity and/or method-level via @PreAuthorize). Provide a default role mapping when file or LDAP auth is used. Include tests covering both roles and anonymous denial.

Extend or create a new HDFS sink module that authenticates to a Kerberized Hadoop cluster using a keytab and principal. Handle krb5.conf and keytab location via configuration, perform Kerberos login before opening the filesystem, write payloads to HDFS, and roll over securely. Includes local Kerberos test setup and tests.

activities.activity_name: U5: Mass Ingestion from Database Systems (Spike)
activities.activity_description: Research and prototype approaches to mass-ingest data from various database systems (beyond JDBC drivers). Evaluate options such as Debezium (CDC), database-specific bulk export tools, Spring Batch, and streaming-based approaches. Collaborate with stakeholders to converge on a design and produce a written design spec document. No production code is committed for this story.

Implement a new HBase sink module using the HBase Java client. Support configurable Zookeeper quorum / HBase configuration, table name, column family, and row-key strategy. Provide PUT batching and error handling. Include unit tests with an embedded/mock HBase and integration test scaffolding.

Implement a sink that writes incoming messages to files on the local filesystem with rolling behavior (size-based and/or time-based). Support configurable directory, file name pattern, rollover threshold, and max history. Include unit tests verifying rollover behavior.

Implement a Spring Integration JMX source that subscribes to notifications from a configurable MBean and publishes them as messages to a channel. Support object name, notification filter, and connection to a remote/local MBean server. Include unit tests.

Wire the new modules into the application, verify that the security layer (file and LDAP, Admin/Viewer roles) coexists with the existing 'jdbchdfs' sink and the new HBase, File Roll, and Kerberized HDFS sinks and JMX source. Run integration tests, fix regressions, and verify endpoints at localhost:9393/.

Update README and module documentation: describe new sinks/sources, security configuration options, sample application.yml fragments for file-based and LDAP auth, and Kerberos/HBase setup notes. Include the U5 design spec as a markdown document.
